newsitem.title: USA: "Bulletproof" penetrates top spot at U.S. box office.
newsitem.headline: "Bulletproof" penetrates top spot at U.S. box office.

text.p: "Bulletproof", a critically panned buddy comedy starring Damon Wayans and Adam Sandler, opened at the top of the U.S. box office with a gross of just $6.0 million, according to studio estimates released Sunday.

Most of the movies in the top 10 suffered large falls in the traditional slump following the Labor Day holiday. The new Whoopi Goldberg movie "Bogus", which also stars French actor Gerard Depardieu, opened in 11th with $1.9 million.

"Bulletproof" is released by Universal Pictures and is the studio's first No. 1 movie since "The Nutty Professor", which opened June 28. According to a Variety poll of critics in New York, Los Angeles, Chicago and Washington DC, four liked "Bulletproof", 10 did not and four were mixed.

The Kevin Costner golfing comedy "Tin Cup" was second for the third week in a row, this time with $4.8 million. "First Kid" remained in third, where it opened last week. It made $4.3 million this weekend. "A Time To Kill" was steady in fourth with $3.9 million.

"The Spitfire Grill", which has been showing in limited release for the past two weekends, launched successfully into wide release this weekend with a $3.6 million gross. This landed it in fifth position vs. 36th last weekend.
